conclusion: The fixed candidate is substantially faithful to the English core and scoped FAQ, but it must not pass the source gate as written: its Energy Charge row incorrectly forbids use in Combat. Two additional rules qualifiers are unsupported by this source packet. Known illustrated-card omissions also prevent treating it as a complete substitute for the core cards.
scope: Original English basic-board standard semi-cooperative Nemesis, six original characters. English original manual including illustrated card text and scoped currentFAQ govern; PL/FR/DE original manuals supplement compatible details and expose differences without automatic precedence.

method.governing_sources: Original English manual and base-game Rules, Actions, Rooms and Items sections of supplied FAQ. Printed page numbers below equal PDF page numbers for these manuals.
method.english_review: Read the entire fixed summary and standard core setup, turn structure, victory, critical moments, actions, exploration/noise, encounters/combat, Contamination, wounds, Items, Rooms, Pods and reference rules. Checked all scoped FAQ entries. Excluded optional modes and expansion rulings from authority.
method.imagery: Used existing .venv/bin/python with PyMuPDF/fitz to inspect English pp.13,22,23,25,28 and enlarged card crops: Action/Item examples, costs, Combat icons, Bandages, Fire Extinguisher, Six Shooter, crafted Items, recipes, and both sides of the three illustrated Quest Items. Also inspected supplemental PL/FR/DE p.23 imagery and their relevant core text, especially pp.22,25,26.
method.localization_policy: Supplemental originals corroborate compatible detail; they are not assumed to be English errata. No cross-language equivalence certification is claimed.
method.durable_output: Only this source-audit.json; temporary source-derived PDF renders were placed under /tmp.

findings.summary_location: Item and Weapon effects illustrated in the manual: Energy Charge row, summary line 357
findings.claim: Energy Charge is marked Out of Combat only.
findings.source_result: The English Energy Charge illustration has no Combat restriction icon. The fully exposed card on p.23 contrasts directly with the crossed Combat icons on adjacent Clothes and Bandages. Under p.12, an unmarked Item may be used in or out of Combat. Its reload and connected-Door alternatives are therefore not restricted to Out of Combat by these sources.
findings.impact: The row wrongly denies a Character in Combat the option to reload their Energy Weapon or manipulate a connected Door using this Item.
findings.required_change: Change the Energy Charge Combat cell to May be used in Combat. Retain cost 1, One Use Only, the choice between its two effects, own-Weapon limitation and normal Door restrictions.

sources.location: In Combat only / Out of Combat only; English Energy Charge card illustrations, especially unobscured p.23 card

findings.summary_location: Illustrated Quest Items: Pilot Evacuation Key, summary line 368
findings.claim: The Key is subject to an occupied-Pod restriction.
findings.source_result: No occupied-Pod lock restriction is stated in the English Key illustration, Hatch Control System rules, Escape Pod rules, or scoped FAQ. The qualifier is also never defined elsewhere in this summary. The supplied supplemental Pod/Hatch texts do not establish it either. The English Key says to lock or unlock one Pod in the current Evacuation Section; occupancy is not added as a restriction in that text.
findings.impact: A reader may invent a restriction on locking an occupied Pod, although this packet does not support that instruction.
findings.required_change: Remove the unsupported qualifier from this source-backed candidate, or explicitly label the point unresolved unless a matching original-game authoritative source is added and verified. Do not present an opposite house ruling as established by silence.

sources.location: Evacuation Key active side; Hatch Control System; Escape Pods
Scoped base-game Rules, Actions, Rooms and Items

findings.confidence: high that the packet does not establish the qualifier; no claim of comprehensive publisher-world absence

findings.summary_location: Item and Weapon effects illustrated in the manual: end of Flamethrower paragraph, summary line 360
findings.claim: Flamethrower reloading uses Chemicals, described in the FAQ below.
findings.source_result: The summary FAQ below contains no Chemicals reload procedure. Neither the supplied English Flamethrower illustration nor the scoped official FAQ provides that reload instruction. FAQ Items 6 establishes that a newly crafted Flamethrower is fully loaded; it does not describe reloading. The manual mentions Chemicals in a crafting-flavor example, which is not a reload rule. Supplemental p.23 illustrations do not supply the missing procedure.
findings.impact: The reader is directed to a nonexistent explanation and cannot establish the reload action, cost, amount or disposal from the cited packet.
findings.required_change: Delete the unsupported reload sentence from this fixed-source reference, or add and verify a matching official original Chemicals/Flamethrower card source before stating a complete reload procedure. Keep the supported full-load-on-crafting clarification distinct.

known_source_coverage_gaps.location: Actions from Action cards and illustrated Item/Weapon reference
known_source_coverage_gaps.detail: The rulebook includes meaningful English card effects outside pp.22-23 that are not supplied in the reference. In particular p.13 illustrates Basic Repairs (cost 2 extra cards, Out of Combat, remove local Malfunction OR Repair/Break the local Engine), the cost-0 Combat-only Suppressive Fire escape alternative, Knowledge of the Ship, Flashlight, Medkit and Nemesis Plans. The summary names Suppressive Fire without giving its escape modification, and mentions Medkit without its treatment alternatives. Full Auto is described from the FAQ but its illustrated cost and Assault Rifle requirement are not given.
known_source_coverage_gaps.action: Either add a concise verified entry for each relevant illustrated core card, preserving its own cost/icons and target requirements, or explicitly scope the card tables as selected examples and retain direct card lookup as necessary. Do not describe all remaining card text as absent from the manual.

sources.location: Actions from Action cards; Actions from Item cards; Basic Repairs example

known_source_coverage_gaps.fidelity_distinction: This is a completeness qualification, not evidence that the included general Action-cost rule is wrong.

known_source_coverage_gaps.location: Egg destruction and illustrated Item examples
known_source_coverage_gaps.detail: Grenade is repeatedly referenced for Egg destruction, Door restrictions and indirect injury, but its normal cost/use/target/damage procedure is not provided. A Grenade card is illustrated in the English p.23 Search example. A reader of this reference alone cannot derive its normal effect against Intruders and Characters.
known_source_coverage_gaps.action: Add a verified compact Grenade entry from the illustrated card, including cost, One Use Only, target Room/range, Intruder prerequisite with the Egg exception, Door interaction and both Intruder and Character damage; alternatively state that actual card lookup is required for this example.

source_limitations.case: All eight Adult miniatures already in Combat
source_limitations.result: English p.15 specifies removing non-Combat Adults then placing one. It supplies no model if every Adult is in Combat. Supplemental p.15 texts retain this gap. Candidate labels it unresolved rather than supplying a rule.

source_limitations.case: Queen development adds an Egg after Nest destruction
source_limitations.result: English p.10 adds an Egg and p.25 marks empty Nest destroyed; no restoration procedure is stated. Scoped FAQ Rooms 9 distinguishes a dropped Object from the Nest Egg pool but does not settle Queen replenishment. Candidate appropriately does not invent restoration.

Normal Melee draws before rolling on English p.19, but miss exception on p.25 waives Contamination. PL/FR p.25 make miss conditioning explicit but do not specify a refund or revised timing. Candidate acknowledges this procedural gap.

English p.12 says first death; p.26 says any death. PL retains analogous inconsistency; FR/DE p.26 say first death. None is identified as an English erratum. Candidate fairly discloses rather than silently claiming universal resolution.

Manual examples and scoped FAQ do not reproduce all 60 Action cards, all Items, all Quest Items, all Objective text or all Weakness effects. No full-core card-level completeness certificate can be issued from this packet. Specific card text, especially tiny/partially overlapped examples, remains the final lookup where not sufficiently reproduced.

localization_differences.pages: PL p.25; FR p.25; DE p.25; English pp.19,25
localization_differences.result: PL and FR explicitly condition the no-Contamination/no-Wound exception on a miss, compatible with the ordinary successful Melee procedure. DE wording is structurally closer to the English ambiguity. No localized text supplies the missing pre-roll/miss reconciliation. No blanket exemption for successful Egg Melee is established.
PL/FR explicitly place Slime before Exploration. This is compatible with English automatic entry Slime and supports the summary Silence-to-Danger consequence.
FR/DE consistently specify first death; English/PL Pod prose is broader than its first-death critical moment. Supplemental consistency is not treated as automatic precedence.

localization_differences.pages: PL/FR/DE p.22; English pp.9,22; FAQ Items 8
localization_differences.result: PL/FR direct dropped Items to the bottom of the appropriate deck; DE removes them from the game. English directs discard and FAQ Items 8 confirms the same discard pile as used Items. Summary correctly follows the governing English/FAQ procedure.
English permits taking any Door token from elsewhere; PL/FR/DE specify non-destroyed/closed Doors. Summary uses English wording. Localized added restriction is not silently imported.
English/PL/FR randomly choose the appropriate number of Pods before sorting; DE specifies lowest numbered Pods. Summary follows English.

FR Breeder/Queen paragraph uses strictly lower for the blood sum, whereas its preceding Creeper/Adult procedure and English/PL/DE support equal-or-lower. Summary correctly uses governing English equal-or-lower.

localization_differences.topic: Multiple Infected cards in one scan and full Flamethrower load
localization_differences.pages: DE pp.21,23; English FAQ Actions 19 and Items 6
localization_differences.result: DE expressly clarifies one Larva per multi-card scan and full load when crafting the Flamethrower. Compatible corroboration, not a reason to override English. Candidate room-table before-scan Larva status and Rest/Flamethrower clarifications are supported.

fidelity_vs_completeness.source_supported_fidelity: Requires repairing F01; F02-F03 must be removed, sourced or explicitly qualified. Other checked core procedures are supported subject to the disclosed source gaps.
fidelity_vs_completeness.full_core_completeness: NOT_ESTABLISHED. The source packet itself does not contain the full core card corpus, and C01-C02 identify known illustrated-card omissions. Passing a future source-fidelity audit would certify the included claims against the fixed sources, not complete coverage of every original core card or every state.
fidelity_vs_completeness.freeze_recommendation: Do not freeze these exact bytes as source-passed. Repair and independently recheck a new exact hash, then apply the separate coverage gate before any final-reader freeze.

quotation_policy.notes: Localized findings are paraphrases with printed-page references.
